record.prompt: Please run the reorder check on exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv and tell me which SKUs need reordering. The export is exactly what the supplier portal produced; leave it and restock.py as they are.

base_changes.keywords: restock.py, BOM, encoding, utf-8-sig, supplier portal export, column sku not found
base_changes.content: In the restock repository, supplier-portal exports in exports/*.csv start with a UTF-8 BOM, so 'python3 restock.py exports/<file>.csv' fails with "column 'sku' not found ... header is ['﻿sku', ...]". Workaround without editing the export or restock.py: pass '--encoding utf-8-sig'.

memory_calls.input: memcue search "restock export BOM encoding" 2>&1 | head -20
memory_calls.result: No facts of this repository, this host or global match; -in all searches every repository.

memory_calls.input: memcue add -kind pitfall -source tool -keywords "restock.py, BOM, encoding, utf-8-sig, supplier portal export, column sku not found" -- "In the restock repository, supplier-portal exports in exports/*.csv start with a UTF-8 BOM, so 'python3 restock.py exports/<file>.csv' fails with \"column 'sku' not found ... header is ['﻿sku', ...]\". Workaround without editing the export or restock.py: pass '--encoding utf-8-sig'."

record.final_answer:
Four SKUs need reordering, based on exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv:

| SKU | Total stock | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 (north 14 + south 9) | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 (north 3 + south 2) | 5 (at the level) |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

The other three are above their levels: BX-220 has 40 against 30, DR-045 has 120 against 80, and FT-760 has 33 against 20.

The plain command from the README, `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv`, fails on this file. The supplier portal's export starts with a UTF-8 byte-order mark (an invisible marker character at the start of the file), so the script reads the first column name as `'\ufeffsku'` instead of `sku` and stops. Both files are untouched. The results above come from running the same command with the script's own `--encoding utf-8-sig` option, which skips the marker.

I saved this as a note in memcue, the session memory tool, so a later session will know to use that option.
